old_description: The product range on standard- and customer tailored connectors of ASSMANN WSW not only convincing by the major variety of different products for so many different applications, but as well by offering appropriate quality, technology and prices in line with market requirements. The big number of standard products, which have been adopted to customer specific requirements and the continuous extension of the product range with new customer tailored connector-systems, show clearly, how important terms like "flexibility" and "customer relation" are for ASSMANN WSW and their success on the market.
about:
Assmann WSW Components Inc. is based in Phoenix, Arizona, where it operates as the U.S. arm of Germany-based ASSMANN WSW components GmbH. The company’s Phoenix facility at 15001 S. 50th Street serves as a sales and support hub for the parent company’s global connector and cable-assembly portfolio.

The company offers a broad range of standard and customized connectors, thermal-management products, and cable assemblies. Its catalog includes board-to-board, wire-to-board, wire-to-wire, circular, D-SUB, USB, FFC/FPC, modular, and power connectors, among others, with thousands of part numbers across categories such as pin headers (6,160 products), wire-to-board (2,288 products), and terminal blocks (2,026 products). Capabilities span multiple pitch spacings (0.3 mm to 17 mm), pin counts up to 100, contact types including crimp, IDC, press-fit, SMT, and solder, current ratings from 0.2 A to 65 A, and straight or right-angle orientations.

While the company does not publicly list specific end markets, its product breadth suggests service to electronics OEMs, industrial equipment builders, automotive suppliers, and telecommunications manufacturers that require reliable interconnect solutions.

Assmann WSW emphasizes flexibility and close customer relationships as core differentiators, highlighting its ability to adapt standard products to custom requirements and continuously expand its portfolio with tailored connector systems. The firm also stresses delivering quality, technology, and pricing aligned with market demands.

name: Assurelink
old_description: AssureLink®, LLC is a locally owned and operated business whose primary goal is to assist the elderly or individuals with unique medical needs live as independently as possible, by offering medical alarms that will summon needed help at the “push of a button”. These alert buttons are available as an In-Home device for those who spend the majority of their time at home or around their house, or as a mobile cellular device for those who get out and about. The mobile unit will work anywhere there is adequate cellular service. Both devices are Medicaid-reimbursable for eligible participants.
about:
AssureLink®, LLC is based in Idaho Falls, Idaho. The company is locally owned and operated, and it was started because the founders cared about individuals who may be faced with losing their independence due to age, disability, or recuperation from a medical condition. No founding year is publicly stated.

The company offers medical alert systems designed to summon help at the push of a button. Its product line includes an in-home device for users who spend most of their time at home, and a mobile cellular device that works anywhere with adequate cellular coverage. Both devices are Medicaid-reimbursable for eligible participants.

AssureLink serves elderly individuals, people with disabilities, and those recuperating from medical conditions. Its customers include those with limited mobility, people living alone, and residents of sparsely populated areas where emergency assistance is not readily available.

The company emphasizes that its Medicaid-reimbursable devices and dual in-home/mobile options set it apart, aiming to ensure customers are never alone.

name: Astemo Americas, Inc. Berea Plant No. 2
old_description: Astemo Americas Joins NVIDIA DRIVE Hyperion Ecosystem as Tier-1 Partner
about:
Astemo Americas, Inc. Berea Plant No. 2 operates in Berea, Kentucky. The facility dates to 1986 and became part of Astemo in January 2021 when Hitachi Automotive Systems, Keihin, Showa, and Nissin Kogyo merged to create a global automotive mega-supplier.

The plant develops and manufactures automotive components including electric powertrains, advanced chassis systems, autonomous driving and advanced driver-assistance systems, and motorcycle systems. It also supplies aftermarket products and provides front-end engineering services. A major expansion of manufacturing operations in Kentucky was announced in 2026.

The company serves automotive OEMs, Tier-1 suppliers, and motorsports teams. It is a Tier-1 partner in the NVIDIA DRIVE Hyperion ecosystem and supports the INDYCAR program with Team Penske and Chevrolet. Its customer base extends to industrial equipment and energy-efficiency sectors.

Astemo was formed to deliver safe, sustainable, and comfortable mobility through advanced technologies. The merger combined the strengths of four companies to accelerate innovations in electrification, autonomous driving, and chassis systems while reducing environmental impact.

about:
Atlantic Poly Inc is based in Norwood, Massachusetts, and was founded in 1981. The company operates as a New England‑based polyethylene supplier and national wholesale distributor of plastic products. Ownership details and founders are not publicly disclosed.

The firm supplies a broad range of polyethylene bags, films, and packaging materials, including custom‑made and printed poly bags, gusseted bags, high‑density and recycled bags, anti‑static and mil‑spec bags, clean‑room and vapor‑corrosion‑inhibitor bags, stretch film, bubble wrap, poly tubing, construction film, dry‑cleaning and garment bags, grocery and shopping bags, and heat‑seal systems. It offers customization services such as custom sizing, printing, and configuration, and states that it handles both small and large orders with no minimum order requirement.

Industries served include medical‑device packaging (clean‑room bags, Aclar bags for long‑term storage), dry cleaning, grocery and retail, construction (vapor‑barrier film), industrial packaging, electronics manufacturing (anti‑static bags and nylon), general manufacturing (wicketed bags for production lines), and trade‑show and event packaging.

The company emphasizes its "Eco‑Green" seal and position as a leader in environmentally friendly packaging, providing recycled and biodegradable options to help customers meet sustainability standards. It also highlights a customer‑service team with a minimum of 15 years of packaging experience and a network of manufacturers to source products it does not produce directly.

name: Atlas Metal Works LLC
about:
Atlas Metal Works LLC operates as a custom metal fabrication house in South Windsor, Connecticut. The company is certified as a Small Business Enterprise by the Connecticut Department of Administrative Services (CT DAS).

The shop provides a range of metalworking services including laser cutting, high-definition plasma cutting, shearing, press-brake forming, CNC punching, plate and pipe rolling, polishing, sawing, and multiple welding processes (MIG/flux-core, TIG, aluminum MIG, spot, and stud welding). Key equipment includes a BLM LS5 12 kW plate laser capable of cutting 5-by-10-foot plates up to one inch thick, a Vectis UR20 cobot welder with 48-inch reach, AccurPress brakes (320-ton and 175-ton), an AccurShear, a Euromac 55-ton CNC punch, a Timesaver 8-inch stainless polisher, Hypertherm and Thermadyne plasma systems, and a Marvel 18-inch automated saw. The company also sells raw stock—sheet, plate, angle, flats, and channel—in full lengths or cut to size, and accepts design files in AutoCAD, FastCAM, or FastSHAPES formats, offering design assistance when needed.

Atlas Metal Works serves commercial clients such as OEM manufacturers, general contractors, construction firms, and other fabrication houses that lack in-house capacity. Its work spans residential, commercial, and industrial projects, with materials including stainless steel, aluminum, carbon steel, galvanized steel, brass, copper, bronze, and mild steel.

The business positions itself as a gap-filler for manufacturers needing supplemental shearing, bending, laser cutting, welding, and hole-punching capacity, emphasizing complete project execution from design through finished delivery.

name: Atlas Wire, LLC
old_description: Atlas Wire, LLC has served the electronic, OEM, and distribution markets since 1966.
about:
Atlas Wire, LLC was founded in 1966 in Itasca, Illinois, and has served the electronic, OEM, and distribution markets for over five decades. The privately held company operates a second production facility in Tucson, Arizona, and is led by President and CEO Bruce Leska.

The company manufactures PVC, cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE), and nylon insulated electrical lead wires in single- and multi-conductor constructions, covering more than 4,900 distinct wire types in sizes ranging from 4 to 30 AWG. Value-added services include spiral striping, extruded longitudinal lines, twisting, heat bonding, respooling, and custom drum or spool packaging. Both facilities maintain tooling for longitudinal line applications, with the Itasca plant offering up to 40% coverage and Tucson up to 30%.

Atlas Wire supplies automotive low-voltage battery cable and primary wire, UL-recognized appliance wire, 600-volt machine tool wire, PVC-insulated building and fixture wire, and military-specification hookup wire for electronic equipment. Its customer base spans original equipment manufacturers, distributors, and the broader electronics sector, with products meeting UL, CSA, automotive, and military standards.

The company describes itself as service-oriented, emphasizing the lowest minimum order quantities, short production lead times, and a willingness to accommodate special requirements. Its quality policy commits to continual improvement, on-time delivery of defect-free products, and compliance with ISO 9001 and IATF 16949:2016.

name: Austin Joinery
old_description: Austin Joinery has worked on two separate projects for me - media storage in an upstairs media room, and a wall-to-wall custom bookcase for my home office. Matt is a joy to work with as he took each project from concept to completion easily, with great communication along the way. The projects themselves were relatively easy to conceptualize - media shelves had to conform to a DVD case's dimensions, and the bookcase "columns" would need to conform to IKEA 30" by 10" shelves. What took the concepts above and beyond were Matt's keen eye and expertise in his field - his rapid feedback from my 3D models helped him understand what I wanted and if any adjustments needed to be made along the way. I couldn't be happier with the results and I would recommend Matt and Austin Joinery time and time again!
about:
Austin Joinery operates from Pflugerville, Texas, in the Austin metropolitan area. The company is owned by Matt, who is identified as the owner in customer testimonials. No founding year is publicly stated, and the ownership structure (family, veteran, woman-owned) is not specified in the available information.

The shop produces custom furniture and built-in cabinetry for residential clients. Projects include dining tables, console tables, bed frames, game tables, hall trees, bookcases, entertainment walls, and replacement table tops. Work is executed in a variety of domestic hardwoods such as red oak, walnut, maple, pecan, and ash, finished with General Finishes stains and Pro-2k clear polyurethane. The process incorporates computer-generated drawings for client approval, and the owner personally oversees each build to maintain quality control. No facility size, headcount, or annual volume figures are disclosed.

Customers are primarily homeowners seeking bespoke pieces, along with interior design firms that collaborate on client projects. Named design partners include Nine Design Group, Cameron Getter Design, and C&H Design Studio, while upholstery work has been coordinated with Rivertown Interiors. The company does not advertise commercial or institutional work.

Testimonials emphasize Matt’s craftsmanship, communication, and willingness to correct previous workmanship errors. Clients describe reasonable pricing for the Austin market and a collaborative design approach that translates 3D models into finished pieces. The company’s stated priority is client service, offering free quotes for custom projects.

about:
Auto Parts Company operates from three Missouri locations: its headquarters in Moscow Mills, just outside the St. Louis metropolitan area, plus yards in Joplin on Highway 43 and St. James on I-44 between St. Louis and Springfield. The company has been in business for decades, though a specific founding year is not disclosed. Ownership details and founder names are not publicly stated.

The company specializes in late-model salvage, dismantling foreign and domestic cars, light trucks, and vans. It sells recycled and aftermarket parts, offers rebuilder services, and also retails late-model vehicles. Customers can order parts online by make, model, part number, or VIN. The operation ships nationwide via UPS or common carrier and provides free delivery to a wide corridor of cities across Missouri, Arkansas, and Oklahoma. A 90-day warranty covers all parts sold.

Auto Parts Company serves the automotive repair and collision industry, as well as individual vehicle owners seeking affordable replacement parts. Its free-delivery zone spans St. Louis, Hannibal, Quincy, Columbia, Jefferson City, Rolla, Springfield, Joplin, Branson, Fayetteville, Tulsa, and Bentonville, indicating a regional focus with national reach.

The company emphasizes its decades of experience, customer service, and the convenience of multiple locations and online ordering as key differentiators. Recent expansion added the Joplin facility to broaden service coverage.
